_sources: research/market-conventions.md — full citations and confidence live there, not here.

page_target.note: The one-page norm is convention repeated across advice sites; no survey-grade source was reached.

summary.note: The US split on summary value is well known in advice writing; no survey-grade source was reached.

photo.note: No UK statute bans a CV photo. ACAS requires equality-monitoring data be kept separate from the CV, which is what produces the norm — but the claim that recruiters discard photo CVs has no primary source.

page_target.note: National Careers Service states no length at all. Two pages is a widely-converged custom without survey backing.

summary.note: National Careers Service frames it as a light "introduction", not a profile paragraph; no evidence on whether it helps.

photo.note: Legally optional under the AGG, and an employer may not require one — but the Lebenslauf tradition held: the Bundesagentur für Arbeit's own templates carry a photo box marked 'keine Pflicht'. The often-quoted ~19% discard figure remains untraceable to any disclosed methodology and is not relied on.

dob.note: Customary, never required. All four Bundesagentur templates carry a Geburtsdatum and all ten samples in its May 2026 guide use one — but that guide's own structural prose omits it, so the convention is drifting. BAG 8 AZR 418/15 found asking age is not by itself an Indiz under §22 AGG.

summary.note: Researched, and the answer is a split: the Bundesagentur places the Kurzprofil on the optional Deckblatt rather than in the Lebenslauf, while its regional 2026 guide recommends one at the top of the CV. No outcome evidence exists in any market.

photo.note: The AMS states a photo 'gilt in Österreich als Standard und wird daher von den Personalverantwortlichen erwartet'. Note this is the employment service's guidance, not law: the Gleichbehandlungsgesetz contains no photo provision at all, and the equality ombuds body flags photos as a documented bias vector without advising against them.

page_target.note: The AMS states a two-page maximum three separate ways, including imperatively. It is guidance rather than an enforced limit, so it stays advisory — but it is the strongest length evidence in the table.

summary.note: Not addressed by the AMS. No outcome evidence exists in any market.

default_language.note: Switzerland has four national languages and the cantons set their own (BV Art. 4, 70). There is no federal definition of the language regions — the BFS assigns them by majority at municipality level, so canton-level inference fails outright: Fribourg and Murten sit in one canton on opposite sides of the line, and bilingual Biel/Bienne is assigned German on a 53/40 split. Null deliberately: the ad's own language decides, and we ask when it cannot.

photo.note: Canton Vaud's official guidance calls a photo 'usuellement exigée' and Canton Bern lists one among the marks of a good CV; the federal SECO page is softer ('gegebenenfalls'). Note the adult-audience Swiss sources are cantonal — the national portal's CV pages address apprenticeship seekers.

page_target.note: Three official sources give three numbers — SECO 'nicht mehr als drei Seiten', Bern '2-3', Vaud '1 à 2' — and the spread follows the language border. Two is the only figure all three permit.

summary.note: Not addressed by any Swiss source reached. No outcome evidence exists in any market.

photo.note: Neither expected nor harmful. The Défenseur des droits has recommended since 2016 that employers not require a photo and 'ne pas écarter un CV qui ne comporterait pas de photographie sur ce seul motif' — an acknowledgement that photo-less CVs were being rejected. France Travail leaves it to the candidate. Default off is supported; the stronger claim that including one is a mistake is not.

default_language.note: Inferred, not sourced. No French institution addresses the language of a CV. L5331-4 bars foreign-language job advertisements for work performed in France, which constrains the employer's ad rather than the candidate's CV.

summary.note: France Travail instructs an 'accroche' — objective plus key skills — at the top of the CV. Shipped optional only because the column's meaning (guidance versus outcomes) is undecided; on a guidance reading France would be expected.

_row.note: No researched row exists for this market. These are neutral least-harm values, not local conventions.

unsupported.JP: Japanese domestic hiring expects a rirekisho (a standardised form with an affixed photo) plus a separate shokumu keirekisho for work history. That is a different document in kind, not a variant of this one. Override if the employer has asked for a Western CV.
